title: Medical Office Replacement Sourcing
name: Medical Office Replacement Sourcing
metaTitle: Medical Office Replacement Sourcing in Dallas, TX
metaDescription: Sourcing medical office replacement property in Dallas for 1031 exchanges: on-campus vs off-campus stock, lease review, and 45-day identification support.

sections.html:
A medical office building looks simple from the outside and gets complicated fast once you're inside the 45-day identification window. Dallas has real medical office stock worth chasing, but the good buildings clear underwriting before most buyers even finish touring them, so sourcing has to start the day your relinquished property goes under contract, not after closing.

The clock on a 1031 exchange doesn't pause for a slow tenant estoppel or a ground lease amendment that takes three weeks to locate, so the sourcing work and the underwriting work have to run at the same time rather than one after the other.

sections.heading: Where the Medical Office Stock Actually Sits
sections.html:
Dallas medical office product clusters around a few identifiable corridors rather than spreading evenly across the metro. The Central Expressway corridor near the Baylor University Medical Center campus carries a mix of on-campus towers and older standalone clinics. Preston Center and Uptown carry newer, smaller-floorplate suites built for specialty practices and dental groups rather than large health systems.

Northwest Dallas and the corridor along Harry Hines have an older stock of single-tenant clinical buildings, often owned by the physician group itself, which changes how a sale-leaseback gets structured versus a straight net-lease deal.

sections.heading: On-Campus Ground Leases vs Off-Campus Fee Simple
sections.html:
On-campus buildings frequently sit on ground leases tied to the hospital system, which affects loan terms and can complicate a straightforward like-kind exchange if the remaining ground lease term is short. Off-campus fee-simple MOB is usually the cleaner replacement asset for exchange purposes because there's no landlord relationship layered on top of the tenant lease.

We flag ground-lease term length, renewal options, and any right-of-first-refusal language before a property ever makes it onto a client's identification list, since that paperwork takes longer to review than most investors expect with the clock already running.

sections.heading: Underwriting the Tenant Base Behind the Building
sections.html:
A medical office building is only as good as the practice groups signed to it. We pull the rent roll apart by specialty, lease expiration, and whether the tenant carries personal guarantees or is backed by a larger physician network. A single-tenant surgical center with eight years left on its term underwrites very differently than a multi-tenant suite full of month-to-month dental practices.

Specialty matters too. A dermatology or dental suite renews on a fairly predictable cycle, while an imaging center or urgent care tenant may have equipment tied to the space that makes relocation expensive for them, which in practice means a stickier tenant than the lease term alone would suggest.

sections.heading: What Gets Screened Before a Candidate Reaches Your List
sections.html:
Before we hand an investor a candidate to put on their identification letter, it clears a fixed screen that looks well past the surface-level rent number:

  • Remaining lease term against the exchange investor's hold horizon
  • Tenant improvement allowance obligations still outstanding
  • Ground lease or reciprocal easement agreements affecting the parcel
  • Parking ratio adequacy for the specialty mix in place
  • Deferred maintenance on clinical infrastructure like backup power and medical gas lines

Medical gas lines and backup power systems in particular carry replacement costs most non-medical investors underestimate, so we surface those figures early rather than letting them appear as a surprise capital item after closing.

sections.heading: Coordinating the Purchase Against Your Exchange Deadlines
sections.html:
Medical office deals tend to move slower than retail or industrial because lenders want more time reviewing tenant credit, and title work on ground-leased parcels takes longer to clear. We coordinate the purchase contract timeline against your 45-day identification deadline and your 180-day exchange period from day one, and we loop in your qualified intermediary early so funds transfer without you ever taking constructive receipt of exchange proceeds.

If a lender needs an extra two weeks to underwrite a physician group's credit, that has to be known before day 45, not discovered after, so the identification letter can reflect a realistic closing timeline rather than an aspirational one.

faqs.q: How fast can a medical office candidate be surfaced after a Dallas property goes under contract?
faqs.a: Sourcing starts the moment your relinquished sale is under contract, not after closing, because the 45-day identification clock doesn't wait. We typically have a working candidate list within the first two weeks so there's room to underwrite before the deadline.

faqs.q: Does an off-campus medical office building still qualify as like-kind?
faqs.a: Yes. Since 2018, like-kind treatment for real property is broad, and an off-campus clinical building qualifies the same way an industrial or retail building would. The bigger question is usually the ground lease structure, not the like-kind test itself.

faqs.q: What lease terms matter most when sourcing MOB replacement property?
faqs.a: Remaining term, whether the tenant carries a personal guarantee or corporate backing, and any early termination rights tied to physician retirement. A short remaining term on a single-tenant building is the most common reason a candidate gets pulled from a list.

faqs.q: Can an ambulatory surgery center or urgent care building qualify as replacement property?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as it's held for investment or business use rather than personal use. These buildings underwrite closer to specialized industrial than to standard office because of the equipment and code requirements built into the space.

faqs.q: What happens if no medical office candidate clears underwriting inside the 45 days?
faqs.a: We keep parallel candidates in other asset classes moving at the same time, since the identification letter allows up to three properties regardless of type. A medical office deal that doesn't clear in time simply gets replaced on the list rather than forcing a rushed purchase.
